rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F_x = F cosθ
F_y = F sinθ
F = sqrt(F_x^2 + F_y^2)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Do not add F and F cosθ as if they were separate extra forces.  ·  sin and cos swap if θ is measured from the y-axis. State the axis.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: θ from the +x axis is the usual choice.  ·  On a slope, resolve weight into mg sinα down the slope and mg cosα into the slope.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Resolution replaces one vector by two perpendicular vectors that add up to it. Along axes at right angles, F_x = F cosθ and F_y = F sinθ, where θ is measured from the x-axis.  ·  The original vector and its two components are not three forces acting at once. The components are a replacement. Using both the original vector and its components double-counts the force.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A negative component is real. It is not dropped.  ·  tanθ alone does not choose the quadrant.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Copy the worked example and hide the result until the last step.  ·  Name the unit of every term in the formula.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A component is zero when the vector is perpendicular to that axis, because cos 90° = 0 or sin 0° = 0. A component is negative when it points along the negative axis.  ·  The magnitude can be rebuilt as F = sqrt(F_x^2 + F_y^2). The direction satisfies tanθ = F_y / F_x, with the quadrant taken from the signs of the components.  ·  Perpendicular components are independent. A force along x does not change the y-equation. That is why a projectile's horizontal and vertical motions are solved separately.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Replacement, not an extra force  ·  The two components replace the original vector.  ·  Resolution of a Vector is based on fundamental principles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Say which axis θ is measured from.  ·  Replace the vector. Do not keep it as well.  ·  Signs come from the quadrant.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Any pair of perpendicular directions may be chosen.
